device.name: iDotMatrix
device.notes:
Multi-size RGB LED pixel-matrix display (text, images, GIF, effects, timers, schedules). No pairing required.
Framed upload protocol — 16-byte header per 4096-byte payload chunk:
  [0-1]  total packet length (uint16 LE)
  [2]    command type: 1=GIF, 2=Image, 3=Text/MultiColor, 6=Phrase
  [3]    sub-type: always 0x00 in framed uploads (sub-type 0x02 exists
         only in the short MultiColor/Phrase commands below)
  [4]    chunk flag: 0=first, 2=continuation
  [5-8]  total data length (uint32 LE)
  [9-12] CRC32 of the entire data payload (java.util.zip.CRC32, LE)
  [13-14] time/delay (uint16 LE)
  [15]   speed/type byte
  [16+]  payload
BLE chunking: 509 bytes when MTU negotiated, else 18 bytes; 20 ms/chunk for GIF/image, 50 ms/chunk for text. Notify response: [?,0,cmd_type,sub_type,status] with status 0=invalid, 1=next-chunk, 2=error, 3=finished. On all hardware-documented units this framed CRC32 upload runs over 0xFA02 together with the short commands below (8none1 btsnoop captures, derkalle4/python3-idotmatrix-library gif.py, Homey docs/idm.md §4.17). Header bytes [0-1] are LITTLE-endian (8none1 decoding_bytes.md: "de 0c" is 0x0cde = 3294 total; derkalle4 to_bytes(2,'little'); Homey §4.17 size_lo/size_hi) — masked on full 4112-byte chunks because 0x1010 is byte-palindromic, it only bites on final/short chunks. Display sizes (ScreenData.getLedSize, app v2.1.4): 1010=10x10, 1001=1x100, 1116=16x11, 1318=18x13, 1619=19x16, 1920=20x19, 2020=20x20 (default), 2010=10x20, 3010=10x30, 3820=20x38 (ScreenData.java:10/49-82). App v2.1.4 knows no 32x32 or 64x64 display code, but square 16x16 / 32x32 / 64x64 panels do exist and use this same IDM-/0x00FA protocol family (derkalle4/python3-idotmatrix-library README, fbnlrz/homeyidotmatrix hardware-verified on IDM-BC5C5F, tomglenn/idx-ai) — an app-vs-firmware gap, not a limit of the hardware. Upload format: every hardware-verified public client uploads an encoded PNG (static) or GIF (animated) FILE, which the device decodes; the device crops rather than resizes (Homey docs/idm.md §5). The app's BGRUtils.bitmap2RGB RGB888 conversion (3 bytes/pixel R,G,B, row-major w*h*3, ScreenData.getdiyImageSize:84-89) is an app-side artifact for its own DIY canvas, not a raw-pixel wire format observed on any unit. Text glyph width varies by device/font. CONFIDENCE: framing header (incl. LE length/delay fields and sub-type=0), CRC32, chunk sizes/pacing, command types 1=GIF/2=Image/3=Text and response format HIGH (hardware-verified on 0xFA02; byte-for-byte confirmed in app v2.1.4 jadx); command type 6=Phrase and image pixel layout MEDIUM (app-derived); the 0xFEE9 service APP-PROVEN-UNUSED (see below). Evidence: 8none1/idotmatrix decoding_bytes.md + btsnoop, derkalle4/python3-idotmatrix-library (const.py, common.py, gif.py), fbnlrz/homeyidotmatrix docs/idm.md (nRF-Connect-verified); app-side jadx v2.1.4: GifAgreement.java:158-208/269-287 (framing, CRC32, response), ImageAgreement.java:141-198 (framing), TextAgreement.java:251-285 (framing), GifAgreement.java:210-240 (509/18-byte chunking), GifAgreement.java:32 / ImageAgreement.java:32 / TextAgreement.java:39 (20/20/50 ms pacing), MutilColorAgreement.java:42-72 + PhraseAgreement.java:39-61 (short-command sub-type 0x02), ScreenData.java (display sizes, DIY image size), BGRUtils.java:41-61 (RGB888), CrcUtils.java:263-270 (java.util.zip.CRC32), BleManager.java:75-78/260 (00FA service + 0xFA02 characteristic).
Short command protocol — service 0xFA02: unframed length-prefixed byte commands ([len, 0x00, cmd, ...]) written to characteristic 0xFA02, with acks/notifications on 0xFA03. This is the protocol every public client (python-idotmatrix, go-idot, Homey) speaks; name prefix "IDM-". App v2.1.4 confirms it: the app configures its BLE library with service 0x00FA and write characteristic 0xFA02 and routes every command through it (BleManager.java:75-78/260); the full short-command set is in BleProtocolN.java.
APP-PROVEN-UNUSED — service 0xFEE9 with characteristics d44bc439-abfd-45a2-b575-925416129600/9601: these UUIDs are merely the shipped defaults of the app's third-party BLE library (cn.com.heaton.blelibrary Ble.Options, Ble.java:354-358); the app overrides them at init with service 0x00FA / characteristic 0xFA02 (BleManager.java:260), so they are dead config in com.tech.idotmatrix. That UUID pair is also a stock NXP BLE-UART demo pair reused by many unrelated products, and no public source has observed it on iDotMatrix hardware. Kept below for completeness — do not rely on 0xFEE9 being present.

credentials.notes: Anything within radio range can connect and issue commands. Physical proximity is the only access control.

factory_reset.effect: No credential state to clear. Power-cycling drops the current connection, which is the actual remedy for the common failure mode: the device already being connected to another central.

steps.action: Remove power (or battery) for a few seconds and reapply.
steps.expect: Device advertises again and accepts a new connection.

methods.description: No provisioning step: the device advertises as soon as it is powered on and accepts a connection from any central. There is no account, no network credential exchange and no pairing PIN, so a replacement client only has to scan, connect and write.

steps.action: Power the device and scan for its advertisement.
Connect and run the documented initialization sequence, if the spec defines one.

setup.notes: No provisioning. The vendor app adds a cloud content library, but none of it is required to connect to and drive the display.

rejoin.notes: Nothing binds this device to a network or an owner, so switching controllers is just connecting from the new one. If the old client is an Android or iOS phone, remove the device from the OS Bluetooth list as well — a cached bond can keep the phone reconnecting automatically and holding the single available link.

characteristics.name: Data Write/Read
characteristics.notes: Library-default write characteristic, unused by the app (overridden with 0xFA02 at init, BleManager.java:260). The framed protocol that would run here — and does run on 0xFA02 — is a 16-byte header (length field at [0-1] is uint16 LITTLE-endian) + up to 4096-byte payload per frame; CRC32 (java.util.zip.CRC32) over the whole data payload. Framing verified on 0xFA02 by 8none1, derkalle4 gif.py and Homey docs/idm.md §4.17; app-side jadx v2.1.4: GifAgreement.java:158-208.

characteristics.name: Data Notify
characteristics.notes: Library-default notify characteristic (Ble.java:358), unused by the app. The transfer-progress response format is verified on 0xFA03; app-side jadx v2.1.4: GifAgreement.java:269-287.

services.name: iDotMatrix Data Service (app-proven-unused)
services.notes: These UUIDs are the shipped defaults of the app's third-party BLE library (cn.com.heaton.blelibrary Ble.Options, Ble.java:354-358); the app overrides them at init with service 0x00FA / characteristic 0xFA02 (BleManager.java:260), so this service is dead config in com.tech.idotmatrix and no public source has observed it on iDotMatrix hardware. The d44bc439-…-9600/9601 pair is also a stock NXP BLE-UART demo pair reused by unrelated products. On all hardware-documented units the framed protocol described here runs over 0xFA02 alongside the short commands.

services.name: iDotMatrix OTA Service
services.notes: Jieli (杰理) OTA stack (com.jieli.jl_bt_ota.* in the app; Jieli's OTA SDK is public as Jieli-Tech/Android-JL_OTA). Not yet unlocked publicly — a session-dependent component is unsolved (235/256 two-byte inputs elicit responses). Evidence: fbnlrz/homeyidotmatrix docs/AE-SERVICE.md (hardware-probed). The app (v2.1.4) bundles two OTA firmware images under assets/ota/ (TR2401R006_01_01_ota_mi.bin, TR2401R007_02_01_ota_mi.bin), so firmware artifacts do exist inside the APK. The hard-coded ASCII AES-256-CBC key with IV = 16 x ASCII '0' (com.heaton.baselib.utils.AESUtils / CloudEncipher) is consumed by the app's cloud HTTP encryption — request/response bodies for manage.heaton.com.cn, including the OTA version-check call (CloudImageManager.java:176-190, CloudAnimManager.java:164-182, OTAUpdataManager.java:204-206) — and is NOT demonstrated to encrypt OTA wire payloads; no wire capture ties it to this service.

eco_mode.description: Eco mode with six config bytes (app v2.1.4 jadx: BleProtocolN.java:33-35; app-derived, not yet hardware-verified — byte semantics unknown)

joint.description: Joint/splice setting for multi-panel setups (app v2.1.4 jadx: BleProtocolN.java:187-189; app-derived, not yet hardware-verified)

locate.description: Locate device. This is a genuinely different frame from the short commands: not [len, 0x00, cmd, ...] but a 16-byte block whose first byte is 0x06 followed by ASCII 'LOCATE' and NUL padding (Agreement.getLocationDevice, jadx v2.1.4 Agreement.java:11-13). The bytes below are the PLAINTEXT — the app does not write them directly: BleProtocol.locationDevice sends getEncryptData(getLocationDevice()), which AES-encrypts the block in place via the native libAES (csh.tiro.cc.aes.cipher, key from keyExpansionDefault) before the single BLE write, so the actual on-wire bytes are the 16-byte ciphertext, not this plaintext. App-derived only; no community/hardware source (CONFIRMATION.md, derkalle4, Homey, 8none1) documents a locate command, so treat as unconfirmed.

mic_rhythm_command.description: Microphone rhythm control; first payload byte is mode+1 per app (app v2.1.4 jadx: BleProtocolN.java:183-185; app-derived, not yet hardware-verified). Shares cmd/sub 0x0B 0x80 with set_mic_type; the device dispatches on the frame's length byte (this one is length 0x06, two payload bytes) rather than on cmd/sub alone.

reset_step_1.description: Factory reset, step 1 of 2 — follow with reset_step_2 (Homey docs/idm.md; found by 8none1)

reset_step_2.description: Factory reset, step 2 of 2 — completes the reset started by reset_step_1

set_fullscreen_color.description: Fill the whole screen with one RGB color (Homey docs/idm.md)

set_mic_type.description: Set hardware microphone type (app v2.1.4 jadx: BleProtocolN.java:80-83; app-derived, not yet hardware-verified). Shares cmd/sub 0x0B 0x80 with mic_rhythm_command; the device dispatches on the frame's length byte (this one is length 0x05, one payload byte) rather than on cmd/sub alone.

set_password.description: Set 6-digit password (000000-999999). Reset device to clear.

verify_password.description: Verify 6-digit password, three 2-digit groups as bytes (app v2.1.4 jadx: BleProtocolN.java:161-173; app-derived, not yet hardware-verified)

characteristics.name: Notify/Ack Data
characteristics.notes: Primarily the notify/ack channel: upload-progress responses and command acks (05 00 <cmd> <sub> 01) arrive here; also readable.

services.name: iDotMatrix Command/Upload Service (0xFA02)
services.notes: The protocol every public client speaks (derkalle4/python3-idotmatrix-library, nj-designs/go-idot, fbnlrz/homeyidotmatrix — hardware-verified). The short length-prefixed commands below and the framed CRC32 upload protocol (16-byte header, length at [0-1] uint16 LE) both run on this service. Additional opcodes from Homey docs/idm.md: set-time 0b 00 01 80 …, clock 08 00 06 01 …, countdown 07 00 08 80 …, chronograph 05 00 09 80 …, scoreboard 08 00 0a 80 …, built-in effects [len, 0, 03, 02, style, 90, count, rgb…], music sync 06 00 00 02 …. Command acks arrive on 0xFA03 as 05 00 <cmd> <sub> 01. App v2.1.4 confirms this configuration byte-for-byte: the app overrides its BLE library defaults with service 0x00FA + write characteristic 0xFA02 (BleManager.java:75-78/260) and sends the full short-command set below from BleProtocolN.java (set-time :26-31, eco :33-35, reset :37-40, brightness :42-45, rotate :57-59, countdown :66-68, chronograph :70-72, scoreboard :74-78, clock :142-144, screen on/off :146-148, speed :133-136, DIY :138-140, color :128-131, password set/verify :150-173, mic :80-87/ 124-126/183-185, joint :187-189; LOCATE in Agreement.java:11-13).
